text.p: The following are the reports carried by Estonia's newspapers on Thursday. Reuters has not verified these reports and does not vouch for their accuracy:
- Finnish students attending Tartu University have launched a court case against the administration, claiming the university violated an agreement when it raised tuition fees.
- The surgical team at Tartu's Maarjamoisa hospital sewed back the hand of a 22-year-old man after it was cut off with a saw.
- Former Interior Ministry chancellor Jaan Toots started a court case against the government, demanding annulment of his dismissal in April for abusing power.
- The government plans to present to parliament a 70 million kroon supplement budget, with 56 million kroons of the sum to go to the government reserve fund, Prime Minister Mart Siimann said.
- Estonia's chances to join the European Union in the first round of expansion are still good, prime minister said on Wednesday.
- The father of a boy who died in a fire at Saaremaa Grammar School in 1995 says he will sue the government for lack of order in an educational establishment.
